policy.interpretation: Provisional source-relative recommendation, not calibrated coding ability or task-success percentage

assumptions: This fixed public reference panel yields a provisional source-relative recommendation, not calibrated coding ability, endpoint performance or task-success probability.

The 50/50 workload weights and tier thresholds are product choices, not measured equivalences. Renormalize over available selected workloads; missing evidence is unknown, not tier C. Confidence is separate from the recommendation index.

Lower numeric priority wins. Select at most one profile/result per workload; metrics in the same source family are fallback choices, not additional votes. Break run ties by latest genuine evaluatedAt, then ascending literal cohort/evaluation/model IDs, never highest score.

Reference distributions are frozen independently of provider offerings. Changes to the provider roster or refreshed source records must not rebuild these panels. A reference distribution update requires an explicit policy-version change and renewed review.

Only the exact admitted cohort IDs and recursive recordConstraints are applicable. Unlisted task releases/configurations cannot inherit this panel and must use another accepted fallback or remain unknown.
Reference runs are deduplicated by exact raw modelId only. Preserve effort, date, precision, version and other label qualifiers; unknown checkpoint aliases are not deduplicated or inferred.

Tier C denotes the lower relative region of the selected reference panel, not absence of coding advantage or evidence of inability. Different source panels are not calibrated to a common capability scale.
Coding category is the arithmetic mean of code_generation and code_completion, requiring both published task columns. This is generation/debugging evidence, not full-repository editing.
Release identifies the task version, not evaluation time. evaluatedAt and taskCount are unknown; literal labels and reviewed identity mappings must preserve reasoning/version distinctions.

Only this single dated release is in the reference distribution; historical and newer releases are not pooled. Newer admitted releases take priority as a product freshness preference, not a score-max choice.

BigCodeBench prefill=false instruct and complete panels are omitted: 14 and 15 distinct model profiles respectively, below minimumReferenceSize=20. Llama-4-Scout's only mapped generation cohort is therefore unsupported; do not relax the gate to assign it a tier.

LiveBench 2025-05-30 and 2024 coding releases are not admitted in v1: the 2026-06-25 and 2026-01-08 panels cover all currently reviewed LiveBench model evidence. Those older cohorts remain distinct task versions, not merged reference records; newly mapped old-only evidence needs a reviewed policy update or another accepted fallback.
LiveCodeBench has no audited snapshot/importer; Arena and SWE-bench are not supported. No reference panel is inferred for them.

This explicitly broader source-family reference panel mixes admitted harness versions/commits, API serving routes, reasoning budgets and edit formats. That comparability is a provisional product assumption, not demonstrated equivalent agent configuration.

Only exact admitted hashed cohorts with test_cases=225, null editor_model/editor_edit_format and no architect format/flag are allowed. Accepted formats: diff, diff-fenced, whole. Missing or partial-task cohorts and architect/editor pairs are not admitted.

Polyglot requires both total_tests=225 and test_cases=225. Python requires test_cases=133 but total_tests/taskCount are unknown in admitted rows; full-suite scope is supported only by the published test_cases metadata, not an inferred known denominator.

Polyglot excludes six rows with test_cases 223/224 and three architect/editor-pair rows (one overlaps a partial-task exclusion). Python excludes 132/33/36/225-task rows; its udiff format is explicitly admitted only in the older Python family.

assumptions: This fixed public reference panel yields a provisional source-relative recommendation, not calibrated coding ability, endpoint performance or task-success probability.

The 50/50 workload weights and tier thresholds are product choices, not measured equivalences. Renormalize over available selected workloads; missing evidence is unknown, not tier C. Confidence is separate from the recommendation index.

Lower numeric priority wins. Select at most one profile/result per workload; metrics in the same source family are fallback choices, not additional votes. Break run ties by latest genuine evaluatedAt, then ascending literal cohort/evaluation/model IDs, never highest score.

Reference distributions are frozen independently of provider offerings. Changes to the provider roster or refreshed source records must not rebuild these panels. A reference distribution update requires an explicit policy-version change and renewed review.

Only the exact admitted cohort IDs and recursive recordConstraints are applicable. Unlisted task releases/configurations cannot inherit this panel and must use another accepted fallback or remain unknown.
Reference runs are deduplicated by exact raw modelId only. Preserve effort, date, precision, version and other label qualifiers; unknown checkpoint aliases are not deduplicated or inferred.

Tier C denotes the lower relative region of the selected reference panel, not absence of coding advantage or evidence of inability. Different source panels are not calibrated to a common capability scale.

Release identifies the task version, not evaluation time. evaluatedAt and taskCount are unknown; literal labels and reviewed identity mappings must preserve reasoning/version distinctions.

Published second-pass pass_rate_2 in a single-model Aider editing harness is preferred over LiveBench's agentic surrogate. It is not full-repository success probability or endpoint-default performance.

This explicitly broader source-family reference panel mixes admitted harness versions/commits, API serving routes, reasoning budgets and edit formats. That comparability is a provisional product assumption, not demonstrated equivalent agent configuration.

Only exact admitted hashed cohorts with test_cases=225, null editor_model/editor_edit_format and no architect format/flag are allowed. Accepted formats: diff, diff-fenced, whole. Missing or partial-task cohorts and architect/editor pairs are not admitted.

Choose one representative per exact raw model label by latest evaluatedAt, then ascending literal IDs. Different effort/format/precision labels remain distinct evaluation profiles even if they could be aliases of one unknown checkpoint; do not strip their qualifiers or select the best-scoring run.

Polyglot requires both total_tests=225 and test_cases=225. Python requires test_cases=133 but total_tests/taskCount are unknown in admitted rows; full-suite scope is supported only by the published test_cases metadata, not an inferred known denominator.

Polyglot excludes six rows with test_cases 223/224 and three architect/editor-pair rows (one overlaps a partial-task exclusion). Python excludes 132/33/36/225-task rows; its udiff format is explicitly admitted only in the older Python family.

providerMetadata.name: DeepSeek: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Free)
providerMetadata.description:
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash is the smallest model in DeepSeek's new architecture family, released September 10, 2026, with native multimodal visual understanding — the production successor to both V4 Flash and the V4 Flash Vision experiment. The new architecture
  targets a higher capability ceiling, faster inference and higher throughput, and DeepSeek reports V4.1 Flash comprehensively surpasses V4 Pro on performance, cost, speed and total task time. It accepts text and images with text output, serves a 1M-token context window with up
  to 384K output tokens, and supports thinking (default, with selectable effort low / high / max) and non-thinking modes across the Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic-compatible APIs, along with JSON output, tool calls and chat prefix completion; FIM works in non-thinking
  mode only. Model weights are open on Hugging Face (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash).

  Official benchmarks at release: 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, 74.2 on DeepSWE v1.1, 65.4 on NL2Repo-Bench, 90.9 on GPQA Diamond, 63.9 on HLE with tools, and strong native-vision agent results (89.6 BabyVision, 78.9 Chartography with tools). Pricing was cut alongside the release:
  $0.15/M input (cache miss), $0.60/M output and $0.003/M on cache hits at off-peak rates, doubling during weekday peak hours (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC); all other hours including weekends are off-peak.

providerMetadata.name: Tencent: Hy3 (Free)
providerMetadata.description: Hy3 is Tencent Hunyuan's production-grade Mixture-of-Experts model — 295B total parameters with only 21B active per pass (192 experts, top-8 routing), the upgraded release built on the Hy3-preview line. It expands RL-training scale and post-training data quality for further gains in reasoning, long-context, and agentic tasks, reaching results comparable to flagship models several times its parameter size. It serves a 256K-token context window (text in, text out) with configurable reasoning effort, and is built for real-world coding, tool use, and multi-step agent workflows at a strong quality-to-cost ratio.

providerMetadata.name: Tencent: Hy4 preview (Free)
providerMetadata.description:
Hy4 preview is Tencent latest Mixture-of-Experts flagship: 770B total parameters with 49B activated per token, 78 layers, 256 routed experts plus 1 shared expert, and a 1M-token context window. It is a text-only model built for coding agents, complex tool-use workflows, and productivity work, with a native MTP layer for speculative decoding.

Reasoning is configurable at three levels (high, low, none) and defaults to high, so it can run as a deep chain-of-thought model for math, coding and analysis, or answer directly when latency matters. It supports native tool calling, structured outputs, and the full sampling parameter set; Tencent recommends temperature 0.9 with top_p 1.0.

Tencent positions it for software engineering, office and data analysis, game prototyping, and scientific research, and reports an internal blind evaluation (163 experts, 203 engineering tasks) in which Hy4 preview averaged 2.99 against GLM 5.3 at 2.92 and Kimi K3 at 2.94. As a preview release Tencent notes known rough edges, including spending longer than necessary on reasoning and over-verifying its own work.

providerMetadata.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety is a compact 4B-parameter multimodal guardrail model from NVIDIA, fine-tuned from Google Gemma-3-4B. It moderates both inputs to and responses from LLMs and VLMs, accepting text and image input and returning text output: a safe/unsafe classification for the user prompt and the response, safety category labels, and an optional reasoning trace. It covers 12 languages with a context window of up to 128K tokens. Suited for prompt and response moderation, content classification, safety pipelines, and enterprise AI guardrails with policy enforcement, and includes a togglable reasoning mode. Part of the NVIDIA Nemotron family of open models for agentic AI.
